newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann at loss to explain share rise.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann at loss to explain share rise.

text.p: German engineering and telecommunicaitons group Mannesmann AG said it could not explain the recent rise in its shares but dismissed speculation of a possible takeover attempt.
"We have no information that anyone is buying a large packet of shares," a Mannesmann investor relations official told Reuters.
The company official said that the most recent study of its shareholder structure showed that the company's capital was still broadly held.
One explanation for the recent interest in the company's shares could be an effort by independent analysts to include the company's investments in fixed-wire telecommunications into their evaluation.
Mannesmann has also conducted a number of roadshows in Switzerland, Asia, Norway, Denmark and Stockholm, the official said.
Mannesmann shares have been rising recently and jumped 2.6 percent to 685.50 marks in pre-bourse trade on Thursday.
In floor trade Mannesmann shares opened at 681.50 and hit a day high of 691.50 marks. At 1115 GMT, the company's shares were trading at 687 marks, up 4.2 percent from Wednesday's close.
Traders speculated that Mannesmann and German energy group Veba AG could be planning to merge their telecommunications business.
